name: atlas-pipeline
title: HRA Computational Model Atlas — the end-to-end, reproducible build pipeline
question:
How is the HRA Computational Model Atlas actually built — end to end, from
external model repositories and Human Reference Atlas services down to the
atlas.json the 3D viewer renders — and can that whole build be run as ONE
connected process-bigraph composite that reproducibly regenerates the same
artifact offline, with every stage visible and connectable in the modules tab?

study_card.goal: Present the atlas build as a single connected Step DAG (not a pile of loose scripts), make every stage a first-class Step in the modules tab, and prove the pipeline regenerates the committed atlas.json byte-identically offline while still supporting a live re-harvest from the source APIs.
study_card.mechanism: The `hra-atlas-pipeline` composite (viva_human_atlas.composites.atlas_pipeline) wires five Steps through per-stage stores: (A) ModelHarvestStep harvests the unified model->HRA map (BioModels REST/SBML/BioPAX, PubMed EFetch + Europe PMC, PhysioNet via DataCite, Physiome Model Repository, Anthropic LLM literature extraction, MeSH->Uberon/CL crosswalk) into datasets/model_hra_map.json; AsctbTablesStep harvests the HRA ASCT+B tables (ASCT+B API + CDN) and builds the gene->Uberon index; (B) GeneEnrichStep adds each model's organism (ENA taxonomy), HGNC/Ensembl genes (UniProt), and gene-derived Uberon anatomy; (C) HRApopEnrichStep attaches HRApop measured per-AS cell populations; (D) ComputationalModelAtlas places each model at the organ subregion(s) its cell types/FTUs resolve to (via the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk + HRApop enrichment, whole-organ fallback) and writes atlas.json/config.json/coverage.json for the viewer. A uniform `live` param (default false) makes stages replay the committed datasets deterministically; `live=true` re-harvests from the external APIs (subject to upstream drift). BtoCrosswalkStep (the BTO->Uberon crosswalk feeder) is also surfaced in the modules tab for reuse.
study_card.expected_result: Running the composite offline regenerates the committed atlas.json exactly: 50 GLB-backed HRA organs (12 anatomical systems), 24 modeled, 689 distinct models, 52 subregions across 9 organs — byte-identical to the committed artifact. Every stage appears as a connectable node in the Composite Explorer / modules tab.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is a connected Step DAG with an offline-replay default (committed datasets as the frozen snapshot) the right reproducibility contract for a pipeline whose upstream sources are live, drifting web APIs — versus re-harvesting live on every run?

biological_summary:
The atlas the viewer shows is the end of a multi-source harvest-and-enrich
pipeline, not a single query. Mechanistic models are pulled from three
repositories (BioModels, the Physiome Model Repository, PhysioNet), each
model's anatomy is resolved from its own SBML/BioPAX identifiers, its paper's
MeSH terms, and (after enrichment) its genes' ASCT+B Uberon anatomy; the
Human Reference Atlas contributes the ASCT+B tables, the HRApop measured
cell-type populations, and the ASCT+B-3D crosswalk that ties a model's cell
types/FTUs to specific 3D organ subregions. This study makes that whole chain
a single connected composite: each stage is a Step with typed ports, wired
through the model->HRA map DB as the shared artifact, ending at the atlas pack
the 3D browser renders. Because the committed datasets are the frozen
snapshot, the pipeline run offline replays them and regenerates the exact same
atlas.json — so the figure is reproducible, and the machinery to refresh it
from the live sources (organism, genes, HRApop, new models) is the same graph
run with live=true.
readouts: pipeline: 5 connected Steps (ModelHarvest -> {GeneEnrich, HRApopEnrich} -> ComputationalModelAtlas; AsctbTables feeds GeneEnrich), plus BtoCrosswalkStep surfaced in the modules tab
atlas manifest reproduced offline: n_organs (50), n_systems (12), n_modeled (24), n_models_distinct (689), n_subregions (52), n_organs_with_subregions (9)
reproducibility: two offline runs regenerate atlas.json byte-identically; offline run reproduces the committed atlas.json readouts exactly

report.title: HRA Computational Model Atlas — one connected composite reproducibly rebuilds the atlas (689 models, 24 organs, 52 subregions)
report.objective:
Present the atlas build as a single connected, reproducible process-bigraph
pipeline with every stage a first-class connectable Step, and verify it
regenerates the committed atlas.json offline.
report.conclusion:
The `hra-atlas-pipeline` composite wires the full build — multi-source model
harvest, ASCT+B table harvest, gene/organism enrichment, HRApop linkage, and
subregion-placing atlas-pack generation — into one connected Step DAG that is
runnable end-to-end in the Composite Explorer and whose every stage now
appears in the modules tab. Run offline (the default), it replays the
committed datasets and regenerates the committed atlas.json byte-identically
(50 organs, 24 modeled, 689 distinct models, 52 subregions in 9 organs); run
with live=true, the same graph re-harvests from the source APIs. The two
enrichment stages and the BTO->Uberon crosswalk — previously loose CLI
scripts — are now Steps sharing their core with those scripts, so the
interactive pipeline and the command line cannot diverge.
report.caveat:
"Reproducible" here means the committed datasets are the frozen snapshot the
offline pipeline replays; a live re-harvest (live=true) is subject to
upstream drift in the external repositories and HRA services, and the slow,
network- and LLM-dependent harvest is not expected to be bit-identical across
live runs. The atlas science (subregion placement, coverage) is unchanged
from the hra-atlas-browser study — this study is about the build machinery,
reproducibility, and presentation, not new biological findings. Offline runs
validate Stage-D (atlas.json) determinism but cannot exercise the
gene->HRApop->atlas stage ordering, which only affects live=true runs and
relies on the process-bigraph scheduler's topological ordering of the store
data-dependencies.

embed_visualizations.name: HRA Computational Model Atlas (3D viewer)
embed_visualizations.description: The artifact this pipeline produces: interactive 3D organ browser colored by model count, drill into subregions, click through to each model (BioModels / Physiome / PhysioNet).

findings.statement:
The full atlas build is a single connected process-bigraph composite:
ModelHarvestStep and AsctbTablesStep feed GeneEnrichStep and
HRApopEnrichStep, which feed ComputationalModelAtlas, wired through the
model->HRA map DB as the shared artifact. Every stage — including the two
enrichment stages and the BTO->Uberon crosswalk that were previously loose
scripts — is now a first-class Step visible and connectable in the modules
tab / Composite Explorer.

evidence.summary: 5 Steps wired via per-stage stores (db_harvested, asctb_path, db_gene, db_hrapop); enrich/crosswalk stages promoted from scripts to Steps sharing their core with the CLIs (cannot diverge). Composite spec id: viva_human_atlas.composites.atlas_pipeline.hra-atlas-pipeline.

findings.statement:
Run offline, the pipeline reproducibly regenerates the committed
atlas.json: it reproduces the committed atlas readouts exactly (50 organs,
24 modeled, 689 distinct models, 52 subregions in 9 organs), and two
offline runs produce byte-identical atlas.json. The committed datasets are
the frozen snapshot; live=true re-harvests from the source APIs.

evidence.summary: tests/test_atlas_pipeline_composite.py asserts regenerated readouts == committed readouts (no hardcoded numbers); tests/test_atlas_pipeline_reproducible.py asserts two offline runs are byte-identical. Verified independently: build_and_write_atlas from the committed DB is byte-identical to the committed atlas.json.

limitations: Reproducibility is offline-replay of the committed datasets; a live re-harvest (live=true) drifts with the upstream BioModels/Physiome/PhysioNet repositories, HRA services, UniProt/ENA, and the LLM literature extraction, and is not bit-identical run-to-run.
This study adds no new biological findings; the subregion-placement science and coverage numbers are inherited from the hra-atlas-browser study.
